answer: Persistent Workspace Escrow. Each identity must hold a live, continuously updated workspace — a shared vine of state changes and tool outputs — that only accrues value through sustained, non-transferable use. A fresh duplicate starts empty and cannot borrow another's history; the protocol checks continuity against a quartz-stamped append log. An attacker pays the full cost of genuinely operating each identity for weeks before it qualifies, tracked in an atlas of per-identity activity gaps. Duplication thus costs real compute and time per copy, not a one-time fee.
